items.title: Verde Árido
items.subtitle: Intelligence and Sustainability in the Semi-Arid Region
items.context: 14th Edition of Campus Mobile — Instituto Claro / USP
items.description: Verde Árido is an Agtech platform aimed at strengthening livestock farming in the Brazilian semi-arid region, selected for the 14th edition of Campus Mobile. The solution addresses the technological management of forage cactus and precision nutrition for herds, seeking to reduce producers' vulnerability to drought periods. The proposal serves both rural producers directly and agricultural consulting firms, with a business model structured to scale. Through georeferencing and the democratization of data such as the Climate Risk Agricultural Zoning, the project offers accessible technical support for decision-making in the field. Its central focus is keeping people on the land and combating rural exodus.

image.alt: Verde Árido app interface showing the forage cactus monitoring dashboard in the semi-arid region

items.title: Guardiões da Bandeira
items.subtitle: Our childhood, turned into a game
items.context: Game Dev Quest — Paraíba Games Incentive Circuit
items.description: Guardiões da Bandeira is a mobile strategy and adventure game selected for Game Dev Quest. The project adapts the popular Brazilian game 'Pega Bandeira' (Capture the Flag) into a competitive digital environment rooted in Brazilian folklore. The interface design was built to support limited-vision mechanics and tactical movement, while keeping navigation intuitive during cooperative matches. The visual identity uses stylized 2D art referencing national culture, blending folkloric characters with special powers. The project includes a progression system, individual rankings, and a soundtrack based on traditional Brazilian rhythms.

image.alt: Guardiões da Bandeira gameplay screen showing a tactical map with characters from Brazilian folklore

items.title: RePlast3D
items.subtitle: 1st Place — Intercourse Competition
items.description: A project awarded 1st place in the inter-course competition at IFPB's Technology Week. The proposal turns plastic waste generated by the institution itself into filament for 3D printing, for use in prototyping labs. The evaluating panel recognized the feasibility analysis as one of the strongest points of the work, along with its environmental impact potential. The project shows how reusing materials can meet real technical demands efficiently and at low cost.

image.alt: Presentation of the RePlast3D project showing the process of turning recycled plastic into 3D printing filament

items.title: Plot Twist Club
items.subtitle: Visual Identity
items.description: Plot Twist Club is an IFPB outreach initiative focused on democratizing access to cinema and encouraging critical thinking among public school students and the local community. With free weekly screenings focused on Brazilian productions, the project drives discussions connecting films to social, historical, and civic issues. I worked on the project's visual identity, including an initial proposal and a revised version.

image.alt: Plot Twist Club visual identity with graphic elements related to cinema and culture

items.title: OnDemand
items.subtitle: UI/UX Design
items.description: OnDemand is an app concept focused on connecting service professionals with clients in a practical way. The work included creating the visual identity — a logo and color palette aimed at conveying trust and agility — and designing the interfaces in Figma. The booking flow was designed to be simple and functional for any type of user.

image.alt: OnDemand app screens showing the service booking flow

items.title: SecureFeed
items.subtitle: Digital Security Platform
items.context: Selection Process — Loopis Junior Enterprise / Team Gamma
items.description: A cybersecurity intelligence platform developed as a team for Loopis Junior Enterprise's selection process. It combines a dynamic cybersecurity news feed (via NewsAPI), a suspicious-link checker integrated with Google Safe Browsing, and an interactive glossary of technical terms. The backend was built in Node.js with Express, keeping API keys secure, while the frontend uses plain HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.

image.alt: SecureFeed platform interface showing the cybersecurity news feed and link checker

items.title: UniRota
items.subtitle: Transportation Management System
items.description: A system built in Java for the Object-Oriented Programming course. The application manages institutional transportation, allowing vehicle and driver registration, route creation, and organization of transit operations.

image.alt: UniRota system interface showing the route and vehicle registration panel

items.title: Consulta Climática
items.subtitle: Web app with API integration
items.description: A web application for real-time weather lookups. Built for educational purposes, it demonstrates consuming external APIs with plain JavaScript — no frameworks — including error handling and a clean, responsive presentation of the data.

image.alt: Consulta Climática app screen showing temperature, humidity, and weather conditions for a searched city

items.title: Pod Adm
items.subtitle: Local Management and Entrepreneurship Podcast
items.context: Final Project, Technical Course in Business Administration — EEEP
items.description: The final project for a technical course in Business Administration, built as a team to connect local business owners with the community of Lavras da Mangabeira (CE). Pod Adm turned conversations about management into accessible content, bringing real stories from local entrepreneurs. I worked on the project's identity and on managing its social media channels (Instagram and YouTube) to expand its reach.

image.alt: Pod Adm cover art with the podcast's business administration visual identity

items.title: Smart Energy
items.subtitle: Energy Consumption Monitoring
items.description: A scientific research project developed in high school that reached the state stage of Ceará Científico. The proposal was a hardware and software prototype capable of measuring the real-time energy consumption of electronic devices and, by cross-referencing that data with utility rates, converting technical readings into monetary values. The goal was to make invisible energy consumption understandable to anyone, promoting more mindful use of resources.

image.alt: Smart Energy prototype with a monitoring board plugged into an outlet and a real-time consumption display

items.title: Semana Literária
items.subtitle: Stage play and graphic design
items.description: A cultural competition among six classes, each presenting a literary work in artistic form. My class placed third. I took part as the play's narrator and contributed to production and graphic design for the project's promotional materials.

image.alt: Documentation of the Semana Literária stage performance with the class on stage

items.title: Feira de Línguas
items.subtitle: Media management and project direction
items.context: EEEP Prof. Gustavo Augusto Lima — 1st Place
items.description: Feira de Línguas was a cultural competition among sophomore classes, organized by the school's languages department. Each class presented cultural aspects creatively — covering history, cuisine, literature, dance, and traditional festivities. My class placed first. I was responsible for managing the project's digital media, creating content for promotional campaigns and coordinating the platforms used to promote the event.

image.alt: Documentation of Feira de Línguas with themed decoration and the winning class's cultural presentation
